result:
The average discount on offline orders in August 2026 was **18.97%**. This is the plain average of `discount_pct` across 14,218 order lines dated 1–31 Aug 2026.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Lines in August 2026 (soft-deleted rows excluded) | 14,218 |
| **Average `discount_pct` per line** | **18.97%** |
| Smallest / largest line discount | 2% / 36% |
| Discount as a share of gross sales at list price (MRP) | 9.84% |

- **Every line had a discount.** None were missing a value or at 0%, so treating missing values as zero wouldn't change the result.
- **The data is consistent.** In the lines I sampled, `net_amount` equals quantity × MRP × (1 − discount_pct/100), so the percentages match the amounts charged.
- **Two ways to read "average discount":** 18.97% is the simple average across lines. Measured in rupees, the discount was only 9.84% of gross sales at list price. The gap means higher-value lines tended to get smaller discounts. Use the 9.84% figure if you mean "how much revenue we gave up."

**Source:** the `offline_orders` table in `sahil-devx.dev_dna_silver` on the `warehouse` connection, via raw SQL. The semantic layer has no average-discount-percentage measure, so I couldn't use it directly. The 9.84% figure follows its `discount_inr` and `gross_revenue_inr` definitions.
